## Data Preparation {visibility="hidden"}

```{python}
#| output: false
import os
import re

import pandas as pd
import yaml

cfg = yaml.safe_load(open("configs/settings.yaml"))
```

```{python}
#| output: false
data_dir = cfg["data_dir"]
county_map = cfg["county_map"]  # "King County" -> id
bare_county_map = {name.replace(" County", ""): name for name in county_map}  # "King" -> "King County"

# OFM sheet name -> component label; column headers span an April-to-April
# period (e.g. "1960-1961") and some Jurisdiction values carry footnote marks,
# so counties are matched on the plain "County" column instead.
OFM_SHEETS = {
    "Residual Net Migration": "Migration",
    "Natural Change": "Natural Increase",
}


def load_ofm_components(file_path):
    """Read the OFM components-of-change workbook's Natural Change and Residual
    Net Migration sheets by county into a long [region, component, year, value]
    frame, attributing each April-to-April period to its ending year to match
    the population estimate it feeds into."""
    frames = []
    for sheet_name, component in OFM_SHEETS.items():
        df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name=sheet_name, skiprows=3)
        df["region"] = df["County"].map(bare_county_map)
        df = df.loc[df["region"].notna()].copy()

        year_cols = [c for c in df.columns if re.search(r"\d{4}-\d{4}", str(c))]
        long = df.melt(id_vars="region", value_vars=year_cols, var_name="period", value_name="value")
        long["year"] = long["period"].str.extract(r"\d{4}-(\d{4})").astype(int)
        long["component"] = component
        frames.append(long[["region", "component", "year", "value"]])
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
```

```{python}
ofm_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
```

```{python}
#| output: false
components_dir = cfg["remi_components_dir"]

COMPONENT_LABELS = {
    "Total Migrants - All Races": "Migration",
    "Natural Growth - All Races": "Natural Increase",
}


def load_remi_components(file_path):
    """Read a REMI components workbook's Migration and Natural Increase rows
    by county (in thousands) into a long [region, component, year, value] frame."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="All", header=5)
    df = df.rename(columns={df.columns[0]: "region", df.columns[1]: "category"})
    year_cols = list(df.columns[3:])

    comp = df[df["region"].isin(county_map) & df["category"].isin(COMPONENT_LABELS)].copy()
    comp["component"] = comp["category"].map(COMPONENT_LABELS)

    long = comp.melt(
        id_vars=["region", "component"],
        value_vars=year_cols,
        var_name="year",
        value_name="value",
    )
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000
    return long
```

```{python}
def load_ofm_population(file_path):
    """Read the OFM Population sheet's April 1 estimates by county into a long
    [region, year, value] frame; column headers end in a year, some with footnote marks."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="Population", skiprows=3)
    df["region"] = df["County"].map(bare_county_map)
    df = df.loc[df["region"].notna()].copy()

    year_cols = [c for c in df.columns if re.search(r"\d{4}", str(c))]
    long = df.melt(id_vars="region", value_vars=year_cols, var_name="period", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["period"].str.extract(r"(\d{4})").astype(int)
    return long[["region", "year", "value"]]

ofm_population_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
ofm_population = pd.concat([ofm_population, ofm_population_region_totals], ignore_index=True)
```

```{python}
#| output: false
# 5-year OFM/SADE/REMI age bins collapsed into 4 broad brackets; the "40-64" bin holds
# the 60-64 5-year bin (up to just before 65), so ages 65+ always fall in the last bracket.
AGE_GROUP_BINS = {
    "0-4": "0-19", "5-9": "0-19", "10-14": "0-19", "15-19": "0-19",
    "20-24": "20-39", "25-29": "20-39", "30-34": "20-39", "35-39": "20-39",
    "40-44": "40-64", "45-49": "40-64", "50-54": "40-64", "55-59": "40-64", "60-64": "40-64",
    "65-69": "65+", "70-74": "65+", "75-79": "65+", "80-84": "65+", "85+": "65+",
}
AGE_GROUP_ORDER = ["0-19", "20-39", "40-64", "65+"]


def load_ofm_age_population(file_paths):
    """Read OFM's age-sex population workbooks (Area Name/Age Group/Year are
    fixed-width, whitespace-padded strings) by county into a long
    [region, age_group, year, value] frame, collapsed into the four broad
    age brackets; the workbook's own "Total" age row is excluded."""
    frames = []
    for file_path in file_paths:
        df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="Population", header=0)
        df["region"] = df["Area Name"].str.strip().map(bare_county_map)
        df["age_bin"] = df["Age Group"].str.strip()
        df = df.loc[df["region"].notna() & df["age_bin"].isin(AGE_GROUP_BINS)].copy()
        df["year"] = df["Year"].str.strip().astype(int)
        df["value"] = df["Total"].astype(float)
        df["age_group"] = df["age_bin"].map(AGE_GROUP_BINS)
        frames.append(df[["region", "age_group", "year", "value"]])
    long = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    return long.groupby(["region", "age_group", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()


def load_sade_age_population(file_path):
    """Read the SADE county age-sex CSV (fills the 2010-2019 gap between the
    OFM intercensal/postcensal workbooks), summing Male and Female per
    county/age bin/year, into a long [region, age_group, year, value] frame
    collapsed into the four broad age brackets."""
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    df["region"] = df["COUNTYNAME"].map(bare_county_map)
    df = df.loc[df["region"].notna() & df["age5"].isin(AGE_GROUP_BINS)].copy()
    df["age_group"] = df["age5"].map(AGE_GROUP_BINS)
    year_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("Total Population ")]
    for col in year_cols:
        df[col] = df[col].astype(str).str.replace(",", "", regex=False).astype(float)
    long = df.melt(id_vars=["region", "age_group"], value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year_label", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year_label"].str.extract(r"(\d{4})").astype(int)
    return long.groupby(["region", "age_group", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()


ofm_age_population = load_ofm_age_population(
    [os.path.join(data_dir, filename) for filename in cfg["ofm_age_sex_files"]]
)
sade_age_population = load_sade_age_population(os.path.join(data_dir, cfg["sade_age_sex_file"]))
ofm_age_population = pd.concat([ofm_age_population, sade_age_population], ignore_index=True)

# "Region" is the sum of the four counties, computed here rather than relying on a workbook total row.
ofm_age_population_region_totals = ofm_age_population.groupby(["age_group", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()
ofm_age_population_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
ofm_age_population = pd.concat([ofm_age_population, ofm_age_population_region_totals], ignore_index=True)
```

```{python}
def load_remi_age_population(file_path):
    """Read a REMI workbook's Population-by-age rows by county (in
    thousands) into a long [region, age_group, year, value] frame,
    collapsed into the four broad age brackets."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="All", header=5)
    df = df.rename(columns={df.columns[0]: "region", df.columns[1]: "category"})
    year_cols = list(df.columns[3:])

    age_bin = df["category"].str.extract(r"^Population - Ages (\d+-\d+|\d+\+) - All Races - Total$", expand=False)
    pop = df.loc[df["region"].isin(county_map) & age_bin.notna()].copy()
    pop["age_group"] = age_bin.loc[pop.index].map(AGE_GROUP_BINS)

    long = pop.melt(id_vars=["region", "age_group"], value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000
    return long.groupby(["region", "age_group", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()


remi_age_population_frames = []
for forecast in cfg["remi_forecasts"]:
    file_path = os.path.join(remi_dir, forecast["filename"])
    df = load_remi_age_population(file_path)
    df["name"] = forecast["name"]
    remi_age_population_frames.append(df)
remi_age_population = pd.concat(remi_age_population_frames, ignore_index=True)

# "Region" is the sum of the four counties, computed here rather than relying on a workbook total row.
remi_age_population_region_totals = remi_age_population.groupby(["name", "age_group", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()
remi_age_population_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
remi_age_population = pd.concat([remi_age_population, remi_age_population_region_totals], ignore_index=True)
```

```{python}
#| output: false
def load_psrc_employment(file_path, year):
    """Read the PSRC major-sector employment CSV (already totaled per county,
    with its own "Region" row) into a long [region, sector, year, value] frame;
    Government and Public Education are summed into a single "Public GovEd"
    sector, since REMI only reports that split as one combined category."""
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, thousands=",")
    sector_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col not in ("Geography", "Total")]
    long = df.melt(id_vars="Geography", value_vars=sector_cols, var_name="sector", value_name="value")
    long = long.rename(columns={"Geography": "region"})
    long["region"] = long["region"].replace(bare_county_map)
    long["sector"] = long["sector"].replace({"Government": "Public GovEd", "Public Education": "Public GovEd"})
    long = long.groupby(["region", "sector"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()
    long["year"] = year
    return long[["region", "sector", "year", "value"]]


psrc_emp_year = cfg["psrc_emp_year"]
psrc_employment = load_psrc_employment(os.path.join(data_dir, cfg["psrc_emp_file"]), psrc_emp_year)
```

```{python}
def load_remi_military(file_path):
    """Read a REMI workbook's Federal Military employment row by county (in
    thousands) into a long [region, sector, year, value] frame; the major-sector
    breakdown below has no Military line, so it's sourced separately here."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="All", header=5)
    df = df.rename(columns={df.columns[0]: "region", df.columns[1]: "category"})
    year_cols = list(df.columns[3:])

    mil = df.loc[df["region"].isin(county_map) & (df["category"] == "Employment - Federal Military")].copy()
    long = mil.melt(id_vars="region", value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000
    long["sector"] = "Military"
    return long[["region", "sector", "year", "value"]]


military_frames = []
for forecast in cfg["remi_forecasts"]:
    file_path = os.path.join(remi_dir, forecast["filename"])
    df = load_remi_military(file_path)
    df["name"] = forecast["name"]
    military_frames.append(df)
military = pd.concat(military_frames, ignore_index=True)

# "Region" is the sum of the four counties, computed here rather than relying on a workbook total row.
military_region_totals = military.groupby(["name", "sector", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()
military_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
military = pd.concat([military, military_region_totals], ignore_index=True)

# Military passes through as REMI's own value, since PSRC's actuals have no counterpart to scale against.
military_actual = military.loc[military["name"] == "REMI", ["region", "sector", "year", "value"]]
```

```{python}
sector_lookup = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, cfg["major_sector_lookup_file"]))


def load_remi_employment_major_sector(file_path, sector_lookup):
    """Read a REMI workbook's employment-by-major-sector rows by county (in
    thousands) into a long [region, sector, year, value] frame, renamed to
    PSRC sector names via sector_lookup; unlike the main REMI workbook, this
    one's categories aren't prefixed with "Employment - "."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="All", header=5)
    df = df.rename(columns={df.columns[0]: "region", df.columns[1]: "category"})
    year_cols = list(df.columns[3:])

    emp = df.loc[df["region"].isin(county_map) & df["category"].isin(sector_lookup["REMI_major_sectors"])].copy()
    emp = emp.rename(columns={"category": "REMI_major_sectors"})

    long = emp.melt(id_vars=["region", "REMI_major_sectors"], value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000

    expanded = long.merge(sector_lookup, on="REMI_major_sectors")
    return expanded.rename(columns={"PSRC_major_sectors": "sector"})[["region", "sector", "year", "value"]]


remi_emp_file_path = os.path.join(cfg["remi_emp_dir"], cfg["remi_emp_forecast"])
remi_major_sector = load_remi_employment_major_sector(remi_emp_file_path, sector_lookup)

# "Region" is the sum of the four counties, computed here rather than relying on a workbook total row.
remi_major_sector_region_totals = remi_major_sector.groupby(["sector", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()
remi_major_sector_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
remi_major_sector = pd.concat([remi_major_sector, remi_major_sector_region_totals], ignore_index=True)
```

```{python}
#| output: false
# REMI's employment figure includes proprietors, which PSRC's actual employment excludes and
# REMI doesn't report separately, so the gap is captured empirically as a ratio at the one year
# both sources cover, then held constant and applied to REMI's forecast.
remi_anchor = remi_major_sector.loc[
    remi_major_sector["year"] == psrc_emp_year, ["region", "sector", "value"]
].rename(columns={"value": "remi_value"})
psrc_anchor = psrc_employment[["region", "sector", "value"]].rename(columns={"value": "psrc_value"})

psrc_ratio = pd.merge(psrc_anchor, remi_anchor, on=["region", "sector"], how="inner")
assert len(psrc_ratio) == len(psrc_anchor) == len(remi_anchor), "Every PSRC/REMI region-sector combo should have a match"
psrc_ratio["ratio"] = psrc_ratio["psrc_value"] / psrc_ratio["remi_value"]

psrc_forecast = pd.merge(
    remi_major_sector[["region", "sector", "year", "value"]],
    psrc_ratio[["region", "sector", "ratio"]],
    on=["region", "sector"],
    how="inner",
)
psrc_forecast["value"] = psrc_forecast["value"] * psrc_forecast["ratio"]
psrc_forecast = psrc_forecast.drop(columns="ratio")

# At the anchor year the scaled forecast should reproduce PSRC's actual value exactly, by construction.
_anchor_check = pd.merge(
    psrc_forecast.loc[psrc_forecast["year"] == psrc_emp_year], psrc_employment, on=["region", "sector", "year"], suffixes=("_scaled", "_actual")
)
assert (_anchor_check["value_scaled"] - _anchor_check["value_actual"]).abs().max() < 1e-6

# PSRC is the actual, observed value at the anchor year; REMI (scaled to PSRC terms) supplies every
# other year. Military has no PSRC counterpart at all, so REMI's value passes through for every year,
# including the anchor year.
psrc_employment_all = pd.concat(
    [
        psrc_employment.assign(source="PSRC"),
        psrc_forecast.loc[psrc_forecast["year"] != psrc_emp_year].assign(source="REMI (PSRC terms)"),
        military_actual.assign(source="REMI (actual)"),
    ],
    ignore_index=True,
).sort_values(["region", "sector", "year"])

pd.concat([psrc_forecast, military_actual], ignore_index=True).sort_values(["region", "sector", "year"]).to_csv(
    os.path.join(output_dir, "REMI_on_PSRC_forecast.csv")
)

with pd.ExcelWriter(os.path.join(output_dir, "REMI_to_PSRC_emp.xlsx")) as writer:
    remi_major_sector.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="REMI Emp by Major Sector", index=False)
    psrc_employment.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="PSRC Emp by Major Sector", index=False)
    psrc_ratio.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="REMI to PSRC Ratios", index=False)
    psrc_forecast.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="REMI on PSRC Forecast", index=False)
```

```{python}
def load_remi_total_employment(file_path, regions):
    """Read a REMI workbook's industry-level Employment rows (excludes the
    separate Employment by Occupation breakdown) summed into a long
    [region, year, value] frame for the given regions."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="All", header=5)
    df = df.rename(columns={df.columns[0]: "region", df.columns[1]: "category"})
    year_cols = list(df.columns[3:])

    emp = df[df["region"].isin(regions) & df["category"].str.startswith(EMPLOYMENT_PREFIX)].copy()
    long = emp.melt(id_vars="region", value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000
    return long.groupby(["region", "year"], as_index=False)["value"].sum()


national_file_path = os.path.join(remi_dir, cfg["remi_national_forecasts"])
remi_national_employment = load_remi_total_employment(national_file_path, ["Nation"]).sort_values("year")
remi_national_employment["growth"] = remi_national_employment["value"].diff()
```

```{python}
def cagr(df, region, start, end):
    subset = df.loc[(df["region"] == region) & (df["year"] >= start) & (df["year"] <= end)].sort_values("year")
    start_value, end_value = subset["value"].iloc[0], subset["value"].iloc[-1]
    n_years = subset["year"].iloc[-1] - subset["year"].iloc[0]
    return (end_value / start_value) ** (1 / n_years) - 1
```

```{python}
#| output: false
def load_ofm_forecast_population(file_path):
    """Read the OFM GMA growth-management forecast's Population sheet, keeping
    the age="Total" row per county, into a long [region, year, value] frame.
    Data points are unevenly spaced (2020, 2022, then every 5 years); the
    first "Projection"-labeled year marks the start of the forecast."""
    raw = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="Population", header=None)
    labels, years = raw.iloc[0], raw.iloc[1]
    year_cols = {int(year): idx for idx, year in years.items() if pd.notna(year)}
    forecast_start_year = int(years[labels == "Projection"].iloc[0])

    df = raw.iloc[3:].copy()
    df["region"] = df[0].map(bare_county_map)
    df = df.loc[df["region"].notna() & (df[1] == "Total")]

    records = []
    for year, col_idx in year_cols.items():
        total_col = col_idx + 2
        sub = df[["region", total_col]].rename(columns={total_col: "value"})
        sub["year"] = year
        records.append(sub)
    long = pd.concat(records, ignore_index=True)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float)
    return long[["region", "year", "value"]], forecast_start_year


ofm_forecast_population, ofm_forecast_start_year = load_ofm_forecast_population(
    os.path.join(data_dir, cfg["ofm_forecast_file"])
)

# "Region" is the sum of the four counties, computed here rather than relying on a workbook total row.
ofm_forecast_population_region_totals = ofm_forecast_population.groupby("year", as_index=False)["value"].sum()
ofm_forecast_population_region_totals["region"] = "Region"
ofm_forecast_population = pd.concat(
    [ofm_forecast_population, ofm_forecast_population_region_totals], ignore_index=True
)
```

```{python}
#| output: false
def load_luvit_population(file_path):
    """Read the LUVit CSV's Region-level Total Population row (in thousands,
    already summed across counties) into a long [region, year, value] frame."""
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    pop = df.loc[
        (df["Main Measure"] == "Population")
        & (df["Detailed Measure"] == "Total Population")
        & (df["Region"] == "Region")
    ]
    year_cols = [c for c in df.columns if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}", str(c))]
    long = pop.melt(value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000
    long["region"] = "Region"
    return long[["region", "year", "value"]]


luvit_population = load_luvit_population(os.path.join(data_dir, cfg["luvit_forecast_file"]))


def load_luvit_employment(file_path):
    """Read the LUVit CSV's Region-level All Sectors w Military employment row
    (in thousands, already summed across counties) into a long
    [region, year, value] frame."""
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    emp = df.loc[
        (df["Main Measure"] == "Employment")
        & (df["Detailed Measure"] == "All Sectors w Military")
        & (df["Region"] == "Region")
    ]
    year_cols = [c for c in df.columns if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}", str(c))]
    long = emp.melt(value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name="value")
    long["year"] = long["year"].astype(int)
    long["value"] = long["value"].astype(float) * 1000
    long["region"] = "Region"
    return long[["region", "year", "value"]]


luvit_employment = load_luvit_employment(os.path.join(data_dir, cfg["luvit_forecast_file"]))
```

## Population Growth by Period {.smaller}

```{python}
remi_base_year = cfg["remi_base_year"]

periods = [
    ("1990s", 1990, 1999),
    ("2000s", 2000, 2009),
    ("2010s", 2010, 2019),
    (f"2020-{history_max_year}", 2020, history_max_year),
    (f"REMI {remi_base_year + 1}-2060", remi_base_year + 1, 2060),
]

def period_avg(df, start, end):
    subset = df.loc[(df["region"] == "Region") & (df["year"] >= start) & (df["year"] <= end)]
    return subset.groupby("component")["value"].mean()

# Historical periods use OFM only, the forecast period uses REMI only.
ofm_periods, remi_period = periods[:4], periods[4]
ofm_avg_table = pd.concat(
    [period_avg(ofm_components, start, end).rename(label) for label, start, end in ofm_periods], axis=1
).T
remi_label, remi_start, remi_end = remi_period
remi_avg_table = period_avg(remi_components, remi_start, remi_end).rename(remi_label).to_frame().T


ofm_pop_region = ofm_population.loc[ofm_population["region"] == "Region"].sort_values("year").set_index("year")["value"]
ofm_growth = ofm_pop_region.diff()

remi_pop_region = remi_population.loc[remi_population["region"] == "Region"].sort_values("year").set_index("year")["value"]
remi_growth = remi_pop_region.diff()


def growth_period_avg(growth, start, end):
    return growth.loc[(growth.index >= start) & (growth.index <= end)].mean()


# Historical periods use OFM only, the forecast period uses REMI only, same split as decade_avg_table.
ofm_growth_avg = pd.Series(
    {label: growth_period_avg(ofm_growth, start, end) for label, start, end in ofm_periods}, name="Avg. Annual Pop Growth"
)
remi_growth_avg = pd.Series({remi_label: growth_period_avg(remi_growth, remi_start, remi_end)}, name="Avg. Annual Pop Growth")

growth_avg_table = pd.concat([ofm_growth_avg, remi_growth_avg]).to_frame().round(0).astype(int)
growth_avg_table = growth_avg_table.rename_axis(index="Period", columns=None)
growth_avg_table.style.format({
    'Avg. Annual Pop Growth': '{:,.0f}'
})
```

## Population Growth by Period — Takeaways

- Historically, growth has been remarkably steady: ranging from **44,341**/year to **55,711**/year.
- The REMI forecast projects **47,714**/year, just below the recent 2020-2026 pace of **48,978**/year.
- No period shows a dramatic acceleration or slowdown — the long-run growth trend persists into the forecast.

## Population Growth by Age Group {.smaller}

```{python}
age_history_max_year = int(ofm_age_population["year"].max())

age_periods = [
    ("1990s", 1990, 1999),
    ("2000s", 2000, 2009),
    ("2010s", 2010, 2019),
    (f"2020-{age_history_max_year}", 2020, age_history_max_year),
    (f"REMI {remi_base_year + 1}-2060", remi_base_year + 1, 2060),
]
age_ofm_periods, age_remi_period = age_periods[:4], age_periods[4]
age_remi_label, age_remi_start, age_remi_end = age_remi_period


def age_growth_series(df, age_group):
    subset = df.loc[(df["region"] == "Region") & (df["age_group"] == age_group)].sort_values("year")
    return subset.set_index("year")["value"].diff()


# Historical periods use OFM/SADE only, the forecast period uses REMI only, same split as growth_avg_table.
age_growth_avg_table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        age_group: (
            [growth_period_avg(age_growth_series(ofm_age_population, age_group), start, end) for label, start, end in age_ofm_periods]
            + [growth_period_avg(age_growth_series(remi_age_population, age_group), age_remi_start, age_remi_end)]
        )
        for age_group in AGE_GROUP_ORDER
    },
    index=[label for label, start, end in age_ofm_periods] + [age_remi_label],
)
age_growth_avg_table = age_growth_avg_table.round(0).astype(int)
age_growth_avg_table = age_growth_avg_table.rename_axis(index="Period", columns=None)
age_growth_avg_table.style.format("{:,.0f}")
```

## Population Growth by Age Group — Takeaways

- The 65+ population has seen the sharpest acceleration — from just **4,506**/year in the 1990s to **23,730**/year in 2020-2025, nearly 5x faster, as the Baby Boomer generation ages into retirement.
- Growth in the 40-64 bracket has fallen just as sharply, from **32,095**/year in the 1990s to **8,914**/year in the 2010s, as that generation aged out faster than it was replenished.
- The REMI forecast expects a more even split across age groups than recent decades, with 40-64 (**16,644**/year) and 65+ (**16,973**/year) growing at a similar pace.

## Comparing Population Forecasts {.smaller}

```{python}
def avg_annual_change(df, region, start_year):
    """Average annual change in value for a region from the first year at or
    after start_year through the series' last year, using only the endpoints
    (handles unevenly-spaced data such as the OFM GMA forecast)."""
    subset = df.loc[(df["region"] == region) & (df["year"] >= start_year)].sort_values("year")
    start_value, end_value = subset["value"].iloc[0], subset["value"].iloc[-1]
    n_years = subset["year"].iloc[-1] - subset["year"].iloc[0]
    return (end_value - start_value) / n_years


forecast_comparison_table = pd.Series(
    {
        "LUV-it (2018)": avg_annual_change(luvit_population, "Region", cfg["luvit_forecast_start_year"]),
        "OFM GMA (2022)": avg_annual_change(ofm_forecast_population, "Region", ofm_forecast_start_year),
        "REMI (2026)": avg_annual_change(remi_population, "Region", cfg["remi_base_year"] + 1),
        "Woods & Poole (2026)": avg_annual_change(
            woods_poole_population, "Region", cfg["woods_poole_forecast_start_year"]
        ),
        
    },
    name="Avg. Annual Population Growth",
).round(0).astype(int).to_frame()
forecast_comparison_table = forecast_comparison_table.rename_axis(index="Forecast", columns=None)
forecast_comparison_table.style.format({"Avg. Annual Population Growth": "{:,.0f}"})
```

## Comparing Population Forecasts — Takeaways

- The 3 more recent forecasts broadly agree, ranging from **40,165** to **46,009** additional residents per year.
- The REMI forecast projects **46,009**/year — the highest of the recent forecasts.

## Summary

- Region population: **4.56M → 6.14M** by 2060 (~0.88%/year).
- Region employment: **2.93M → 4.04M** by 2060 (~0.89%/year).
- Migration is overtaking natural increase as the primary source of population growth.
- The region is forecast to keep outpacing the nation in overall job growth.
- Recent population forecasts agree within a **40,000-46,000** person/year range.
